definition: A refinement of scaling laws showing that many large language models had been undertrained relative to their size, and that model size and training tokens should scale roughly equally.
details: The Chinchilla paper argued that, for a fixed compute budget, better performance is achieved by training a smaller model on more data than by training a larger model on less data, reshaping how subsequent LLMs were trained.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Boil it down and it is this: A refinement of scaling laws showing that many large language models had been undertrained relative to their size, and that model size and training tokens should scale roughly equally. Here is why it matters: The Chinchilla paper argued that, for a fixed compute budget, better performance is achieved by training a smaller model on more data than by training a larger model on less data, reshaping how subsequent LLMs were trained. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. That blueprint is Chinchilla Scaling.
